_about: Every ESP32-P4 board outside the catalog, for /boards/all/. Read from schematics and vendor pages, not hardware. Marks: y = has it (camera: takes a Raspberry Pi camera ribbon), n = does not, ? = not known. verdict: candidate | maybe | no | terminal. The catalog boards (_boards/) are added by the build and need no entry here. ribbon = a short label for the camera connector.

kvm.name: Wireless-Tag WT32P4C5-43S
kvm.note: New in October 2026. 15-pin camera connector in Raspberry Pi order, Wi-Fi through a C5, microSD. Not known yet: which GPIOs drive the camera's I2C. It carries a 4.3" screen ESP-KVM would not use.

kvm.name: Wireless-Tag WT99P4C5-S1
kvm.note: IP101 Ethernet and a C5, microSD. The 22-pin camera connector's pinout is not published.

kvm.name: Wireless-Tag WT9932P4C61-TINY
kvm.note: Wi-Fi only. 15-pin camera connector in Pi order, high-speed USB on its own Type-C. Not stated: how the C61 talks to the P4.

kvm.name: Wireless-Tag WTDKP4C5-S1
kvm.note: Sold with 16 or 32 MB PSRAM; take the 32. The guide contradicts itself about the camera connector, there is no microSD, and Ethernet needs a PHY on the header.

kvm.name: Makerfabs MaTouch ESP32-P4 7" and 10.1"
kvm.note: A C6, microSD, Ethernet on the 10.1". Both ship an SC2336 camera on the camera connector; whether it takes a Pi ribbon is not said.

kvm.name: MakerGo / Osprey ESP32P4C5
kvm.note: 15-pin camera connector and a C5, but Ethernet only as RMII pins on a header: wired network needs your own PHY board.

kvm.name: OspreyPi / Maker Go ESP32-P4-Mini v2.0
kvm.note: A C6, microSD, a Type-C labelled high-speed USB. The camera connector looks wired for a camera module (its own 2.8 V and 1.8 V supplies), not in Pi order.

kvm.name: Guition JC1060P470 (7", Ethernet version)
kvm.note: A C6, microSD, Ethernet and a camera on one variant. Too little is published about the camera connector, flash and USB.

kvm.name: M5Stack Stamp-P4
kvm.note: The camera is on a board-to-board connector (needs an adapter), there is no PHY, and Wi-Fi needs the C6 add-on.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-Touch-LCD panels
kvm.note: A C6, microSD, no Ethernet. The 3.5" one has a camera built in; for the others the camera connector is not stated.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-M
kvm.note: Looks like the ESP32-P4-WIFI6 with a rev 1.x chip and a 4-pin USB header, so the WIFI6 image may simply run. Not verified.

kvm.name: RELOC SCINTIX P4
kvm.note: A compute module for Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5 carrier boards, with Ethernet and a C6. The camera comes from the carrier, and the USB is described as host. No schematic yet.

kvm.name: Elecrow CrowPanel Advanced 5", 7", 10.1"
kvm.note: A C6 in a swappable slot and a USB device port. The camera is optional, on Elecrow's own connector.

kvm.name: Olimex ESP32-P4-PC
kvm.note: Everything else is right, but a USB hub sits on the high-speed port, so it is always a host and can never be the target's keyboard.

kvm.name: Olimex ESP32-P4-DevKit
kvm.note: The high-speed USB lines are not brought out anywhere; its Type-C is the serial bridge.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-Pico, ESP32-P4-Core-DEV-KIT
kvm.note: No network at all: no Ethernet PHY and no Wi-Fi co-processor.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-86-Panel-ETH-2RO
kvm.note: The camera connector is not fitted on this variant.

kvm.name: LILYGO T-Display-P4
kvm.note: The camera is built in; there is no free camera connector.

kvm.name: Seeed reTerminal D1001
kvm.note: The camera is built in; there is no free camera connector. A good terminal candidate, below.

kvm.name: Espressif ESP32-P4-EYE, ESP32-P4X-EYE
kvm.note: Camera kits: the camera connector carries their own sensor.

kvm.name: M5Stack Tab5
kvm.note: Not as a KVM: the camera connector holds its own camera. It runs ESP-KVM terminal instead, as a handheld screen for a KVM.

kvm.name: LILYGO T-Halow P4
kvm.note: 8 MB of PSRAM. USB and Ethernet come out only on the M.2 edge, with no PHY and no socket for the target, and the 24-pin camera connector has no 3.3 V and a 1.8 V I2C.

kvm.name: Adafruit Metro ESP32-P4 Hydra
kvm.note: 16 MB of PSRAM and a rev 1.x chip. The high-speed USB comes out on a Type-A host port with its own 5 V supply, the Type-C is full speed. A C6 for Wi-Fi, no Ethernet. No schematic yet.

kvm.name: JetKVM Mini
kvm.note: A finished KVM on an ESP32-P4X with 32 MB of PSRAM and 16 MB of flash: HDMI in, high-speed USB-C to the target, 100 Mbit Ethernet, a 240x240 screen and a microSD slot. The capture chip and the pins are not published, and there is no schematic. Its optional secure boot takes signed firmware only, so other firmware needs it left off.

kvm.name: JetKVM Mini W
kvm.note: The Mini with an ESP32-C5 for Wi-Fi 6 (2.4 and 5 GHz) in place of Ethernet. The same unknowns: capture chip, pins, how the C5 is wired to the P4.

terminal.name: M5Stack Tab5
terminal.note: What the terminal is built and tested on. The Keyboard for Tab5 clips on.

terminal.name: Espressif ESP32-P4 Function EV Board
terminal.note: It already runs ESP-KVM, so one board could be both ends.

terminal.name: Guition ESP32-P4-M3-Dev
terminal.note: The same board also runs ESP-KVM itself.

terminal.name: Seeed reTerminal D1001
terminal.note: 32 MB PSRAM and a 2500 mAh battery. The closest to the Tab5 of the lot.
